# What gets built

The fact the test plan already determines — per criterion, whether a break was named and what it is — becomes two fields of the researcher's structured return, and the workflow renders them into every reviewer dispatch. Nothing about what the reviewer *does* with them is added here; that is increment 2.

## The shape: two lists of strings, not one list of objects

`breaks` and `unbreakable`, both `array` of `string`.

- `breaks` — one entry per acceptance criterion the test plan named a break for, in the form `<criterion> — <the production change that would make its test fail>`.
- `unbreakable` — one entry per acceptance criterion the test plan named no break for, in the form `<criterion> — <why no test can catch it>`.

Rejected: a single `array` of `{criterion, break}` objects. `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs`'s `smallValue()` (line 366) keeps a return field in the index only when it is a boolean, a number, a string of at most 500 chars, or an array of at most 50 strings of at most 500 chars each; an array of objects is classed as content and dropped. A resumed run rebuilds its steering from that index alone (`recorded` map, agile-loop.js line 686), so an object list would reach no resumed reviewer and would force a change to the shared helper and its suite. Two string lists survive the existing projection untouched, and they mirror `checks`, which already travels this exact route.

Rejected: one list with `no break:` written inside the string. Which list an entry is in is the answer to "whether", so it belongs in the shape, not in prose the reader has to parse — and increments 2 and 3 both branch on that answer.

## 1. `workflows/agile-loop.js`

(a) **`PLAN`** (the researcher's dispatch schema, ~line 274). Add `breaks` and `unbreakable` after `checks`, each `{ type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }` with a description in the style of the `checks` one beside it: what one entry is, its form, and that the reviewer reads nothing the researcher wrote so this is how the break reaches it. Add both names to `required`.

(b) **`PLAN_PAYLOAD`** (~line 448). Insert `'breaks'` and `'unbreakable'` after `'checks'`, so the researcher is told to record them into `backlog.json` beside the rest of its return. That is also what puts them where the index projection can find them after a crash.

(c) **`INDEX_STEP`** (~line 110). Add `breaks` and `unbreakable` as array-of-string properties with descriptions in the shape of the `checks` one ("The step return's `breaks` when the index carried them. Empty otherwise."), and add both to `required`. Without this the state-loading agent is not asked for them and a resumed run's reviewer is handed nothing.

(d) **A renderer beside `checkList`** (~line 481), `breakList(breaks, unbreakable)`. It returns, with these three sentences verbatim — the tests assert on them, so do not reword:

  - when `breaks` is non-empty, the line `The break the plan named for each criterion it named one for:` followed by one `  - <entry>` line per entry, exactly as `checkList` renders a command;
  - when `unbreakable` is non-empty, the line `The criteria the plan named no break for, with the reason:` followed by one `  - <entry>` line per entry;
  - when both are empty, the single line `No plan named a break for any criterion of this increment.`

When only one list is non-empty, only that list's heading and entries are rendered. Give the function a comment saying why it exists: the reviewer reads no run state, so a fact the plan already settled reaches it through its prompt or not at all.

(e) **Per-increment carrying.** Declare `let lastBreaks = []` and `let lastUnbreakable = []` inside the increment loop, beside `let plan = null` (~line 974) — *not* at module scope beside `lastChecks` (line 907). Set them from `plan.breaks` / `plan.unbreakable` with an `Array.isArray` guard at the same place `lastChecks` is set (~line 1040). Comment the difference: `lastChecks` deliberately crosses increment boundaries because a command judges whatever code is in front of it, while a break names a criterion and criteria belong to one increment — carrying them would hand an increment worked `direct` the breaks of the increment before it.

(f) **The reviewer dispatch** (~line 1174). Add `breakList(lastBreaks, lastUnbreakable) +` immediately after `checkList(lastChecks) +`. It goes into every review round, not round 0 alone: `scope()` gives every round the increment's whole criteria list, and the round that accepts an increment is frequently a correction round, which is precisely where the issue measured the cost.

**Do not** add the block to the implementer dispatch (~line 1113). The implementer reads the plan out of the state and no criterion of this increment asks for it there.

## 2. `agents/researcher.md`

One new bullet in `## What you record`, directly after the `needsTests`/`checks` bullet (lines 61-63). It carries three rules and nothing else:

- the two fields and what each holds, each with its template written out: `<criterion> — <the production change that would make its test fail>` for a `breaks` entry, `<criterion> — <why no test can catch it>` for an `unbreakable` entry;
- that every acceptance criterion of the increment stands in exactly one of the two lists;
- that where the plan needs no tests at all, every criterion of the increment stands in `unbreakable`.

Write it as a recipe stating the output, per `.claude/rules/authoring.md` row 3: the failure being prevented is an omitted required element, and the repair is the slot plus the template, never a prohibition. State each of the three once — the `## The test plan` section must not repeat any of it, because two wordings of one rule drift.

Two phrases are forbidden in the new text: `counts as tested` and `dependency footprint`. `test-repo.sh` asserts that the shared brief is the only agent page or shipped skill carrying either, and a researcher page that used one would turn those ownership cases red.

## 3. `README.md`

Line 83's reviewer row says the reviewer is "handed nothing any other role produced". It is already loose — the reviewer is handed `checks` — and this change makes it falser. Reword that one cell so it is true of what the reviewer is handed: the commands and the plan's breaks, never the plan itself. This adds no rule, so it needs no `test-repo.sh` case.

## What is deliberately not touched

- `agents/reviewer.md`. Increment 2 owns every rule about what the reviewer does with a break or with an unbreakable criterion. This increment only makes the fact arrive.
- `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs` and its suite. The two-string-list shape was chosen so that file needs no change at all.
- `rulebook.md`. Increment 3 owns the session's report.
- The run result (`worked` entries). Increment 3 owns it.

## Where they go, and the conventions

Every case lands in `/home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh` (bash; the workflow cases run inside the node driver that file writes to a temp dir and executes). The command that runs just that file is `bash test-repo.sh`.

**There is no suite doc for this file, and none is to be written.** `test-repo.sh`'s own case at line 2154 requires a `CLAUDE.md` only of directories holding a `*.test.mjs`; `test-repo.sh` sits at the repository root, and a `CLAUDE.md` there would load as project memory and be inherited by every subagent the session dispatches — exactly what `.claude/rules/agents.md` says must never happen in this checkout. So the conventions you need are here instead:

- A section opens with a bare `echo` then `echo "=== <lowercase title>"`. A case is an `if`/`else` reporting through `ok "<declarative sentence>"` and `no "<what is wrong>"`.
- Every case carries a comment above it naming the criterion it proves and, verbatim, the break that turns it red. Follow the style of the cases at lines 473-550.
- A case about a page's prose greps a collapsed copy of that page (`tr '\n' ' ' | tr -s ' '`), because the prose wraps. Each section declares its own collapsed variable; do not reuse `researcher_form`, which the `=== ... winning form` section at line 3035 owns.
- A workflow case is a driver mode: add the fixture near its neighbours, add the mode to `contextFor()` (line 1005), add an `else if (mode === 'wNN')` branch in the assertion chain, and register it with a `run_driver "$wf" wNN "$wf_name: <title>"` line in the loop at lines 1812-1843. Any new `MARKER-` string goes into `DISJOINT_MARKERS` (line 722); the harness itself asserts no marker is a substring of another.
- The driver records `{label, agentType, prompt, schema}` per dispatch, so a case may assert on the dispatched schema object directly. The pattern to copy is w8 (line 1305).

Put the page cases in a **new section** placed immediately after `=== the mutation standard has one owner` (i.e. before line 551), titled along the lines of `=== the break the test plan named reaches the reviewer`.

## The cases

### Criterion 1 — the structured return names, per criterion, whether a break was named, and carries it

1. `The researcher's structured return names the break per criterion` — a new driver mode (call it w31) with a plan fixture that names no break; assert `byLabel('research:i1.0').schema.properties.breaks.type === 'array'`, the same for `unbreakable`, and that `schema.required` includes both → the research dispatch demands both fields — break: delete either property from `PLAN.properties` or either name from `PLAN.required` in `workflows/agile-loop.js`.
2. `The researcher is told to record both lists` — same mode; assert the research prompt contains the rendered bullets ``- `breaks` `` and ``- `unbreakable` `` → the payload list names them — break: remove either name from `PLAN_PAYLOAD`.
3. `agents/researcher.md gives both lists their template` — collapsed page grep for `<criterion> — <the production change that would make its test fail>` and for `<criterion> — <why no test can catch it>` → both templates stand on the page — break: delete the new `breaks`/`unbreakable` bullet from `## What you record`.
4. `Every criterion stands in exactly one of the two lists` — collapsed page grep for that sentence → the coverage rule stands — break: delete that sentence from the bullet.
5. `A plan that needs no tests puts every criterion in unbreakable` — collapsed page grep for that clause → the needs-no-tests edge is decided on the page and not left to judgement — break: delete that clause from the bullet.

(Cases 3, 4 and 5 are also the whole of criterion 3: the only page rules this increment adds are those three, all on `agents/researcher.md`. The README cell is a claim, not a rule, and gets no case.)

### Criterion 2 — the workflow carries the criteria and their breaks into the reviewer's prompt

6. `The reviewer's prompt carries the break the plan named` — extend mode **w6**: add `breaks: ['does i1 — MARKER-BREAK']` and `unbreakable: []` to the shared `planReturn` fixture (line 758), then assert the reviewer's prompt contains `MARKER-BREAK`, contains the criterion text `does i1`, and contains the heading `The break the plan named for each criterion it named one for:` → the block reaches the reviewer — break: delete `breakList(lastBreaks, lastUnbreakable) +` from the review dispatch. Retitle w6's `run_driver` line, which currently claims the reviewer's prompt carries "the checks alone".
7. `The reviewer's prompt carries a criterion the plan named no break for` — mode w31, with a fixture whose `breaks` is `[]` and whose `unbreakable` is `['does i1 — MARKER-UNBREAKABLE']` (model it on `planReturnWithQuestion`, line 766); assert the reviewer's prompt contains `MARKER-UNBREAKABLE` and the heading `The criteria the plan named no break for, with the reason:`, and does **not** contain the breaks heading → the unbreakable half travels and is labelled as itself — break: drop the `unbreakable` half of `breakList`, or render both lists under one heading.
8. `A correction round's reviewer is given them too` — extend mode **w10** (its round-1 review is `review:i1.1`); assert that call's prompt contains `MARKER-BREAK` → the block is not round-0 only — break: guard the `breakList(...)` call on `round === 0`, or move it into the non-correction branch of the review prompt.
9. `A resumed run's reviewer is given the break the state recorded` — extend `idxStep()` (line 809) with `breaks: Array.isArray(r.breaks) ? r.breaks : []` and the same for `unbreakable`, which flows the fixture through `resumeState()`; then in mode **w2** assert the `review:i1.0` call's prompt contains `MARKER-BREAK`, beside the existing `CHECK-MARKER` assertion → the break survives the replay path the resume uses — break: read the lists off a freshly dispatched plan only, e.g. by setting `lastBreaks` inside a `round === 0` branch that a replayed step skips.
10. `The state loader is asked for both lists` — mode w31, in the shape of w8's loader assertions (line 1341): assert `byLabel('load-state').schema.properties.runSteps.items.properties.breaks` exists and `...items.required` includes `breaks`, and the same for `unbreakable` and for `increments.items.properties.steps.items` → a resumed run is actually given them, which the fixture-driven case 9 cannot catch because the stub returns its fixture whatever the schema says — break: remove either property from `INDEX_STEP`, or either name from its `required`.
11. `A direct increment is not handed the previous increment's breaks` — extend mode **w21** (a full increment followed by a direct one): assert the `review:i2.0` prompt does **not** contain `MARKER-BREAK` and does contain `No plan named a break for any criterion of this increment.` → the lists reset at the increment boundary — break: declare `lastBreaks`/`lastUnbreakable` at module scope beside `lastChecks` (line 907) so they carry across increments.
12. `A run with no researcher step yet tells the reviewer so` — extend mode **w20** (one increment, cut direct, no researcher ever dispatched): assert the `review:i1.0` prompt contains `No plan named a break for any criterion of this increment.` → the empty-list edge renders the sentence rather than an empty heading or nothing — break: return `''` from `breakList` when both lists are empty.

### Criterion 4 — `bash test.sh` exits 0

No case of its own: it is the check command below, and its exit code is the criterion.

## What is left untested, on purpose

- The wording of the README cell. It is a claim on a front page, not a rule, and pinning marketing prose with a grep buys a false alarm on the next rewrite.
- The exact prose of the two `breakList` headings beyond the verbatim strings cases 6, 7, 11 and 12 already assert.

## What is already red

Nothing was run. No decision in this plan turned on a fact only a run could settle: the shape of the two fields follows from `smallValue()` as it is written, the placement follows from the dispatch sites, and the suite's conventions follow from the file. The check list below is unrun — the first run of it belongs to whoever runs it downstream.
rulings: Carried the fact as two arrays of strings, `breaks` and `unbreakable`, rather than one array of {criterion, break} objects, because backlog.mjs's steering projection keeps only arrays of short strings and drops objects as content, so an object list would not survive a resume and would force a change to the shared helper and its suite; wrong costs re-shaping two schema entries and one renderer.

Rendered the break block into every review round rather than round 0 alone, because the reviewer that finally accepts an increment is usually a correction round's and that is exactly where the issue measured the cost; wrong costs a few extra prompt lines in each correction round.

Reset `breaks` and `unbreakable` at the increment boundary instead of carrying them across it the way `lastChecks` is carried, because a break names a criterion and criteria belong to one increment; wrong costs a direct increment's reviewer being told no break was named where the previous increment's would have been shown.

Added no rule to agents/reviewer.md, because what the reviewer does with a break or an unbreakable criterion is increment 2's whole subject; wrong costs one increment in which the reviewer is handed a prompt block its page does not mention.

Wrote no CLAUDE.md suite doc for test-repo.sh and put its conventions in the test plan instead, because the repository requires a suite doc only of directories holding a *.test.mjs and a CLAUDE.md at the root would load as project memory inherited by every subagent, which .claude/rules/agents.md forbids; wrong costs the conventions living in the run state rather than in a doc.

Included the one-cell README fix to the reviewer row, because this change makes its "handed nothing any other role produced" claim falser and a stale claim left standing is a finding waiting to be filed; wrong costs one table cell to revert.
